title: Expected value & variance
subtitle: The two numbers behind every trading decision

sections.title: Expected value
beats: Expected value (EV) is the long-run average result if you repeat a bet many times.
Recipe: multiply each outcome by its chance, then add them up.
Positive EV means you win over time, even if you lose often.
Worked: 40% chance to win $30, 60% chance to lose $10. EV = 0.4×30 − 0.6×10 = $6 per bet.
sections.example: A carnival game that costs $2 and pays $10 one time in 10 has EV = $1 − $2 = −$1. The house wins.
sections.sayback: Tell someone why a strategy that loses 60% of the time can still make money.

quiz.a: Break even over the long run.

sections.tieback: Liquid Bot: 'expectancy' on your scorecard is exactly EV per trade.

sections.title: Variance & standard deviation
beats: Variance measures how spread out results are around the average.
Recipe: for each result, take (result − average) squared. Average those.
Standard deviation is the square root of variance. It's back in dollars, so it's easier to read.
Worked: results 2, 4, 6. Average 4. Squared gaps 4, 0, 4. Variance = 8/3 ≈ 2.67. SD ≈ 1.63.
sections.example: Two drivers both average 30 min to work. One is always 29–31, one swings 10–50. Same EV, very different variance.
sections.sayback: Why can two strategies with the same EV feel totally different?
sections.tieback: Liquid Bot: high variance = deeper drawdowns. That's why you start with small size.
